articles.title: The one change that worked: Anxiety had me hiding from the world – then two magic questions set me free
articles.summary: I used to be terrified of socialising, certain I would embarrass myself the moment I opened my mouth. And as for dates … As with a lot of teenagers, social confidence was not my strong suit.
body: What I now know to be social anxiety I dismissed as just nerves at that young age. Although I knew something wasn’t quite right, for most of my early teens I managed to disguise my discomfort. Sharing a friendship group with my twin sister meant I could hide behind my sibling.

As we got older, the disparity started to grow and her flourishing social confidence magnified my lack of it. By my late teens, I often found myself building up social situations to an unbearable point. The false narrative I’d created of embarrassing myself socially had begun to completely overshadow my desire to be around other people. So I hid away a lot.

My mum found me a therapist. She was phenomenal and talked me through a lot of emotions that I didn’t really understand. When the end of my therapy sessions neared and we had spoken as much as we could, all that was left to do was for me to go out into the world and put into practice everything we had discussed.

As with a lot of teenagers, social confidence was not my strong suit.

articles.title: ‘Whose job is it to empty the dishwasher?’ Experts on the conversations every couple needs to have
articles.summary: Burnout or breakup are constant dangers when one partner carries too much of the mental load of looking after the home and family. Here’s how to spread the burden more evenly.
body: Many households have an imbalance in domestic duties, and women often struggle from carrying the weight of the organisational side of life. Here, mental load experts share the secrets to having a more equitable home – and the rewards that can be gained from it.

Leah Ruppanner, a professor of sociology at the University of Melbourne and the author of Drained: Reduce Your Mental Load to Do Less and Be More, says that mental load burnout is a precursor to physical burnout. If you are organising everything, explains Ruppanner, you can’t enjoy life because you are constantly thinking about what is happening next. The first step is accepting how it is affecting you: handily, Ruppanner has created a website – lightenlab.com – where you can measure your mental load and get advice on how to manage it.

articles.title: Is it true that … double-dipping food is unhygienic?
articles.summary: This practice does transmit mouth bacteria, but don’t panic. Double-dipping means eating part of a piece of food and then putting it back into a communal dip – for example, biting a carrot and dipping it into shared hummus, or redipping a half-eaten tortilla chip in salsa.
body: “You do transmit bacteria from the food you have eaten back into the source,” says Prof John Tregoning, the author of Live Forever? A Curious Scientist’s Guide to Wellness, Ageing and Death. He points to a study testing salsa, chocolate sauce and cheese dip, which found bacteria were transferred to all three, with salsa showing the most contamination.

But does that make people sick? “I doubt it, because the other person is going to have their own bacteria,” he says. Most people’s mouth bacteria are relatively stable and can fight off bacteria introduced from someone else. The risk may be higher for someone who is severely immunocompromised or who has recently taken antibiotics, but such infections are likely to be rare.
He says we should be more worried about bacteria transferred via hands. Studies of shared foods such as popcorn have shown a small amount of cross-contamination from fingers to food to mouths.

articles.title: Sex, drugs and floral fabrics: Celia Birtwell relives her wild times – and wilder outfits – with Ossie Clark
articles.summary: They dressed – and partied with – the innermost in-crowd. As a swirling new show celebrates their fashion creations, Birtwell recalls her happy days with Clark and her sorrow at the loss of David Hockney.
body: I n the mythical age of bohemia, the psychedelic decade between Mary Quant’s cheerful miniskirts and the first snarls of punk, Celia Birtwell and Ossie Clark were London’s most fashionable couple. Birtwell created the fabrics: daydreamy, botanical doodles that captured the idealism and looseness of the times in wisps of chiffon. Clark magicked these into sensual bias-cut dresses with a freewheeling grandeur that was part Hollywood glamour, part rock’n’roll anarchy.

More than just designers, they were a whole vibe. They dressed – and partied with – the innermost of the in-crowd. Talitha Getty, Marianne Faithfull and Anita Pallenberg hung out at Quorum, their Chelsea boutique. At a catwalk show in 1970, there were two Beatles, Cecil Beaton and Brigitte Bardot in the audience – and, after Clark began making stage clothes for Mick Jagger, he accompanied the Rolling Stones on tour. David Hockney’s portrait of the couple in their pomp – Mr and Mrs Clark and Percy, painted two years into their marriage, when Birtwell was pregnant with their second child – sealed their place in the mythology of the period.
points: They dressed – and partied with – the innermost in-crowd.
As a swirling new show celebrates their fashion creations, Birtwell recalls her happy days with Clark and her sorrow at the loss of David Hockney.

articles.title: Joseph Altuzarra’s Old Navy Collection Is as Romantic and Feminine as You’d Imagine
articles.summary: Florals, plaid, and Fair Isle–the designer shares with Vogue the inspiration behind his fall capsule. Shop the collection now, exclusively on Vogue for 24 hours.
body: Windswept hair, a scarf draped over one shoulder, a Fair Isle knit made for the moors of Scotland. Designer Joseph Altuzarra’s latest collaboration with Old Navy is a world plucked straight out of Wuthering Heights, one you want to transport yourself to and spend fog-banked mornings roaming around in a parka. “It's romantic, it's feminine, it's a real wardrobe,” the designer shares with Vogue. “There's a real kind of feeling of romanticism and melancholy,” he adds.

Take the scarf bias dress, its print reading like a silk scarf worked into the silhouette—Altuzarra calls it one of the collection's standouts, alongside the denim, offered in “a wide-leg boyfriend cut and a slightly flared, patch-pocket style,” according to the designer. “The denim has already been really popular in the office.”

articles.title: The 10 Best Airbnbs in Kyoto for a Fall Getaway
articles.summary: The best Airbnbs in Kyoto feature tranquil water features, elevated Japanese design, and central locations—here, 12 spots currently on our wishlist.
body: There’s something about Kyoto in the fall, when ginkgo leaves turn a vibrant shade of yellow, and maple leaves morph from green to orange before settling into a deep red. Yes, cherry blossom season is pretty as a picture, but during October and November, the city comes alive in an equally magical way. Kyoto’s temples—of which there are many—are some of the best places to witness the true extent of kōyō (fall foliage), often set within large landscaped gardens that are at their peak this time of year. Kiyomizu-dera and Kōdai-ji are two of the most popular, but for something a bit more zen, seek out those in more rural areas, like Rakuhoku.

Kyoto is more traditional and slower-paced than Japan’s capital, Tokyo, or its neighbor, Osaka: rich historic districts, centuries-old temples, and groomed gardens stand in for sleek skyscrapers and neon lights. You could easily spend a full week here, roaming both the residential machiya-lined streets and ticking off all the touristy must-sees. And for a taste of local life, consider staying in an Airbnb.

articles.title: Cottage Cheese Meatballs
articles.summary: Protein on protein on protein. Great on their own or stirred into tomato sauce.
body: Adding cottage cheese to a meatball might sound like an attempt to cram extra protein into a recipe, but it’s not the only valid reason. Something magical happens with the addition of cottage cheese: It practically disappears in the baking process, lending the meatballs juiciness and a subtle savory-salty flavor. As a bonus, the cottage cheese helps to stretch the recipe and you’ll end up with almost twice as many meatballs from one pound of ground beef.

Think of this recipe as a bit of a blank canvas, allowing you to use the meatballs however you please. You can bake them and pop them in your mouth as is, drop them into simmering tomato sauce, or stuff them between slices of bread for a hearty sandwich. They, like most meatballs, are also very meal-prep-friendly and take to freezing well.
More great cottage cheese recipes this way: Cottage Cheese Lasagna; Cottage Cheese Caramelized Onion Dip; and Roasted Honeynut Squash With Cottage Cheese and Chili Crisp.

articles.title: The 18 Best Airbnbs in Rome for an Italian Escapade
articles.summary: From the trendy neighborhood of Monti to the quintessential charm of Trastevere, here’s where to stay in the best Airbnbs in Rome.
body: When the 1st-century poet Tibullus referred to Rome as Urbs Aeterna (which translates to “ Eternal City ”) he couldn’t have imagined that his remarks would remain the city’s most infectious marketing phrase over two thousand years later. Rome, indeed, is a city with serious lasting power. And no matter how many times you’ve visited over the years, this ancient destination, with all its perfect piazzas and crumbling ruins, never fails to leave you wanting more. Thankfully, the best Airbnbs in Rome make it all the easier to explore nooks you’ve never experienced before—from your very own slice of local life.

For travelers eager to immerse themselves in the city’s culture, these Roman rentals plant you in the middle of the most exciting neighborhoods. For a warren of medieval streets lined with traditional food, book a flat in Trastevere. In search of an elegant, upscale vibe? Try Prati. Or perhaps you’re after a trendy setting that’s both laidback and full of locals; Monti is great for that. You’ll find there’s plenty of diversity to satiate every sort of traveler.
points: From the trendy neighborhood of Monti to the quintessential charm of Trastevere, here’s where to stay in the best Airbnbs in Rome.

articles.title: MTV VMAs 2026 Fashion: Taylor Swift, Tyla, Charli XCX & More Arrive on the Red Carpet
articles.summary: See what your favorite musicians and performers wore on the red carpet at the 2026 MTV VMAs.
body: On September 27, the 2026 MTV VMAs —one of the biggest nights in music—took place at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, honoring some of the best albums, music videos, and live performances of the last year.

Leading the list of nominees were acts including Madonna, Bruno Mars, Sabrina Carpenter, Ariana Grande, and Taylor Swift (who also recieved the VMAs’ inaugural Artist Director Honors); and among those who took the main stage to perform were Charli xcx, Lisa, Teddy Swims, Shaboozey, Gunna, Kacey Musgraves, and Yung Lean.

But before host Snoop Dogg kicked off the show, the red carpet served up plenty of statement looks—from the dark, witchy glamour of people like Charli (in Saint Laurent) and Teyana Taylor (in Zuhair Murad couture) to the ultra-low-rise stylings of Tyla (in straight-off-the-runway Mowalola ) and Sombr (in custom ERL).
Below, see what all your favorite musicians wore to hit the red carpet at the 2026 MTV VMAs.
